relationships.relationship_explanation: The MOEM section Evidence Determination Methodology – Step 4: Consider Organizational and Regulatory Requirements supports this AI RMF subcategory by providing a structured implementation approach for incorporating applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, and organizational requirements into the determination of operational evidence needed to demonstrate AI governance.

The MOEM section Governance Evidence supports this AI RMF subcategory by identifying the operational evidence that organizations may use to demonstrate implementation of AI governance policies, processes, procedures, assigned responsibilities, and documented governance decisions that incorporate trustworthy AI characteristics.

The MOEM section Risk Tier Classification supports this AI RMF subcategory by providing a representative risk-informed approach for determining the level of operational evidence appropriate to support AI governance based on organizational risk tolerance, system context, and governance requirements.

The MOEM section Evidence Determination Methodology supports this AI RMF subcategory by providing a structured implementation approach for determining the operational evidence needed to demonstrate that AI governance processes, governance controls, and governance outcomes have been executed in accordance with organizational risk priorities.

The MOEM section Evidence Lifecycle supports this AI RMF subcategory by describing how operational evidence is maintained, reviewed, retained, and managed throughout the AI governance lifecycle, enabling ongoing governance monitoring and periodic review of governance activities and outcomes.

The MOEM section Risk Tier Classification supports this AI RMF subcategory by providing a representative risk-informed approach for determining the level of operational evidence appropriate for AI systems based on organizationally defined risk priorities. While MOEM does not establish AI system inventory mechanisms, it supports consistent evidence determination once AI systems have been identified.

The MOEM section Evidence Lifecycle supports this AI RMF subcategory by describing how operational evidence is retained, managed, and appropriately disposed of throughout the AI governance lifecycle, helping preserve governance continuity and accountability as AI systems evolve or are retired. MOEM does not prescribe AI system decommissioning procedures but supports management of the operational evidence associated with those activities.

The MOEM section Role-Aware Evidence Responsibilities supports this AI RMF subcategory by defining responsibility for generating, maintaining, validating, reviewing, and using operational evidence across governance and operational roles.
